description: Emergency power system 96-hour fuel supply required; written load-shedding plan required and submitted with construction documents
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER (OH-EP-001): The electrical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} do not demonstrate compliance with the emergency electrical system requirements of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-16 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by the Ohio Department of Health (ODH). The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) the generator fuel storage capacity has not been specified or demonstrated to provide a minimum of 96 hours of continuous operation at full essential electrical system load without resupply; and/or (2) a written load-shedding plan identifying which non-critical electrical loads will be sequentially dropped in the event of a prolonged emergency has not been included in the submission. Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-16 requires both provisions for all licensed hospitals. Construction documents that omit or inadequately address emergency power requirements will not be approved by the ODH Plans Examination Section, and the project may not proceed to construction until these deficiencies are resolved.
fix_template:
1. Provide a generator sizing calculation on the electrical drawings or in the specifications demonstrating that the on-site fuel storage system (including tank capacity plus any permanent piping connections to a bulk fuel delivery system) is sufficient for 96 continuous hours of operation at the calculated full essential electrical system load; include a load schedule tabulating all connected essential loads.
2. Specify the automatic transfer switch (ATS) performance: confirm that each ATS serving Type 1 essential electrical system loads (life safety and critical branches) transfers within 10 seconds of normal-power failure per NFPA 110 and FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-8.3.
3. Prepare and include in the construction documents a written Load-Shedding Plan identifying all non-essential and deferrable loads served by the emergency generator; organize loads by priority tier and document the sequence and method (manual or automatic) by which each tier will be shed under sustained emergency conditions.
4. Confirm on the site plan that the generator fuel tank location, secondary containment, vent pipe terminations, and fill-point access comply with Ohio EPA and local fire department requirements; note the 30-day testing and fuel-level inspection schedule in the O&M section of the specifications.
5. Resubmit revised electrical drawings, load calculations, and Load-Shedding Plan to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for continued review and approval.

description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room required with negative pressure, minimum 12 ACH, and direct exhaust to outdoors
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / VENTILATION (OH-INF-001): The mechanical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room ventilation requirements of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-35 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1 as adopted by ODH. The submitted mechanical drawings and/or air-balance schedule do not confirm one or more of the following mandatory requirements: (1) each AII room must be maintained at a continuous negative pressure differential with respect to the adjacent corridor and all connecting spaces; (2) a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (ACH) must be provided, with all exhaust air discharged directly to the building exterior and not recirculated to any other space; (3) the exhaust discharge point must be located and detailed to prevent re-entrainment into any air intake per ASHRAE 170-2021. Failure to provide properly designed AII rooms places patients and staff at risk for airborne pathogen transmission and will result in denial of ODH construction approval.
fix_template:
1. Add pressure-relationship diagrams to the mechanical drawings showing a minimum negative pressure differential of -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) in each AII room relative to the adjacent corridor and all connecting vestibule or anteroom spaces; specify continuous monitoring via a visual pressure indicator (magnahelic gauge or electronic monitor) visible from the corridor.
2. Revise the air-balance schedule to confirm a minimum 12 total air changes per hour in each AII room; identify supply CFM, exhaust CFM, and net pressure relationship for each room and provide a room-by-room summary table on the mechanical drawings.
3. Route all AII room exhaust ductwork to dedicated exhaust fans that discharge directly to the building exterior; show the exhaust fan locations and duct routing on mechanical floor plans and roof plan, and confirm that discharge points are a minimum of 25 feet from any operable window or air intake per ASHRAE 170-2021 and local jurisdiction requirements.
4. Specify that no air from the AII room exhaust system is recirculated to any other space; if a heat-recovery device is used on the exhaust system, specify a non-cross-contaminating type (run-around coil or rotary wheel with purge sector) and provide documentation of the manufacturer's leakage performance.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings, pressure-relationship diagrams, and air-balance schedule to the ODH Plans Examination Section in Columbus for review and approval; coordinate with the facility infection preventionist to document ICRA measures during construction.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control 2003

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net; 20 ACH total; humidity 20-60 percent; temperature 68-75 degrees F required
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SURGICAL SUITE / HVAC (OH-SU-001): Review of the architectural and mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County reveals noncompliance with the operating room design standards required by Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-37 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by ODH. One or more of the following mandatory requirements have not been met: (1) the net clear floor area of one or more operating rooms is less than the required minimum of 360 square feet, exclusive of fixed and moveable equipment; (2) the air-balance schedule does not confirm a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour; (3) the HVAC design does not specify or demonstrate maintenance of relative humidity within the 20% to 60% range; and/or (4) the temperature control specifications do not confirm maintenance of a temperature range of 68°F to 75°F when the OR is in use. All four requirements are mandatory under OAC 3701-83-37. Documents with unresolved OR deficiencies will not receive ODH approval.
fix_template:
1. Add net clear floor area calculations for each operating room to the architectural floor plan; confirm a minimum of 360 square feet net, measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall and excluding fixed casework, columns, equipment bays, and structural projections; revise room dimensions or layout as needed.
2. Update the air-balance schedule on the mechanical drawings to list for each OR: supply air CFM, exhaust air CFM, total ACH, outside-air ACH, and pressure relationship (positive with respect to all adjacent spaces); confirm a minimum 20 total ACH and minimum 4 OA ACH per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
3. Specify humidity monitoring and control: include a humidifier and dehumidification capability in the AHU or in-room, sized and controlled to maintain RH between 20% and 60% at all occupied times; specify BAS alarms for RH values outside this range and document a response protocol.
4. Specify temperature control system capable of maintaining 68°F to 75°F in each OR under full surgical load and all seasons; provide equipment schedules confirming sensible cooling and heating capacity; specify thermostat locations inside the OR and confirm that nursing staff can request setpoint adjustments within the permitted range.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans and mechanical drawings, including the updated OR air-balance schedule, AHU equipment schedule, and HVAC control sequence, to the ODH Plans Examination Section for review and approval.

description: Minimum 100 SF single-occupancy patient room; 80 SF per bed double-occupancy; in-room toilet required for ICU patient rooms
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM / ARCHITECTURAL (OH-PR-001): The architectural construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not comply with the minimum patient room area requirements and toilet access standards of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-32 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by ODH. The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) one or more single-occupancy patient rooms appear to provide less than 100 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of toilet rooms, closets, vestibules, and alcoves; (2) one or more double-occupancy (two-bed) rooms appear to provide less than 80 square feet of clear floor area per bed space; and/or (3) one or more patient rooms designated as intensive care unit (ICU) beds do not provide an in-room toilet and handwashing station within the room envelope as required by OAC 3701-83-32 for ICU settings. These standards are prerequisites for ODH facility licensure and must be addressed in revised construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Provide net clear floor area calculations on the architectural floor plan for every patient room; confirm single-occupancy rooms are 100 SF minimum and double-occupancy rooms provide 80 SF per bed space, measuring from finished face of wall and excluding toilet rooms, closets, lockers, vestibule areas, and fixed equipment footprints.
2. Revise any non-compliant rooms by adjusting room dimensions, removing non-essential fixed elements from the room footprint, or reconfiguring the floor plan; clearly dimension all revised patient rooms on the submitted drawings.
3. For all ICU patient room positions, confirm that a private toilet room with water closet and handwashing sink is provided within the room envelope and accessible without entering a public corridor; show the toilet room on the floor plan with interior dimensions and confirm ADA-compliant accessible clearances per the 2010 ADA Standards as adopted in Ohio.
4. Verify that all patient toilet rooms comply with Ohio plumbing code (OPC) requirements for fixture supply and drain connections; confirm handwashing sinks in patient rooms meet ODH infection control standards with hands-free (sensor or wrist-blade) operation specified in the plumbing fixture schedule.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans with room-by-room area calculations and annotated toilet adjacency diagrams to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for review and approval.

description: Ohio Fire Code Chapter 19 healthcare occupancies; NFPA 101-2021 and NFPA 13 automatic sprinklers required throughout
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY (OH-FLS-001): The fire protection and life safety construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Ohio Fire Code (OFC) Chapter 19 governing healthcare occupancies, the 2021 edition of NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code) as adopted by ODH, and NFPA 13 (Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems). Specifically, the submitted documents do not adequately confirm: (1) that an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 13 is provided throughout the entire facility, including all mechanical spaces, storage rooms, and interstitial areas; (2) that the fire alarm system meets NFPA 72 requirements with full coverage notification appliances and voice evacuation; and/or (3) that the construction type, occupancy separation, corridor fire ratings, and exit access travel distances comply with NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18 for new healthcare occupancies or Chapter 19 for existing healthcare occupancies. ODH will not issue plan approval for healthcare facilities with unresolved fire and life safety deficiencies.
fix_template:
1. Provide complete NFPA 13 sprinkler system drawings including: a site and floor-plan layout showing all sprinkler head types and locations, hydraulic calculations with water supply analysis, riser diagram, and a specification section referencing the NFPA 13 edition being applied; confirm full building coverage including all storage, mechanical, and interstitial spaces.
2. Submit NFPA 72 fire alarm system drawings including initiating device locations, notification appliance layout, mass-notification or voice-evacuation system design, fire alarm control panel (FACP) location, and a complete system narrative; confirm supervised automatic sprinkler water-flow and tamper-switch monitoring.
3. Provide a code analysis on the drawings or in a separate code compliance narrative demonstrating compliance with NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18 (new) or Chapter 19 (existing): confirm construction type, occupancy classification, compartmentation (smoke compartment areas ≤ 22,500 SF), fire-rated corridor construction, exit access travel distances, and suite arrangements.
4. Coordinate with the Ohio State Fire Marshal's Office (OSFM) and local fire department for separate fire protection system permits; provide ODH with a copy of the OSFM or local fire department approval before ODH issues a final construction approval.
5. Resubmit coordinated fire protection, fire alarm, and architectural code-compliance drawings to the ODH Plans Examination Section and confirm that the local Authority Having Jurisdiction has been notified of the project.

description: Ohio Department of Health plan review required; submit to Columbus office before beginning construction on any licensed healthcare facility
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PLAN REVIEW / GENERAL (OH-GEN-001): This comment is issued pursuant to Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-05, which requires that construction documents for the new construction, substantial renovation, or alteration of any ODH-licensed healthcare facility be submitted to and approved by the Ohio Department of Health Plans Examination Section before construction may begin. A review of the submission package for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} indicates that the submittal is incomplete. One or more of the following elements are missing or deficient: (a) a completed ODH Building Project Registration form; (b) design professional seals and signatures from licensed Ohio architects and engineers of record on all discipline drawings; (c) a project description or program statement identifying the scope of work, affected licensed occupancy, bed count changes, and project cost; and/or (d) evidence of a concurrent local building department permit application. Beginning construction without a written ODH plan approval is a violation of OAC 3701-83-05 and may result in a Stop Work Order, required correction of non-compliant work at the owner's expense, and delay of ODH facility licensure.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit the ODH Building Project Registration form available on the ODH Health Care Regulation website; include the ODH facility license number, facility address, name of the owner's representative, total estimated construction cost, and names of all licensed Ohio design professionals of record.
2. Ensure all construction drawings are sealed, signed, and dated by a licensed Ohio architect (architectural drawings) and licensed Ohio professional engineers (structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection drawings) per Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4703 and Chapter 4733; unlicensed or out-of-state seals require a specific authorization from the applicable Ohio licensing board.
3. Prepare a written project description covering: project type (new construction, addition, renovation, change of use), affected departments, scope of licensed services impacted, any change to licensed bed count or service types, phasing plan, and estimated construction schedule.
4. Submit three (3) paper sets of complete construction documents (or electronic submission through the ODH e-Plans portal) to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, 7th Floor, Columbus, OH 43215; include all architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, and civil drawings, together with specifications and energy compliance documentation.
5. Submit a concurrent application for a local building permit to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) having local building code enforcement jurisdiction over the project site; provide ODH with a copy of the local permit application receipt, and do not begin construction until both the ODH written approval and the local building permit are in hand.

description: Certificate of Occupancy from local AHJ and ODH survey required before the facility may open or expand licensed services
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — LICENSURE / CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY (OH-GEN-002): This comment is issued as advance notice of the two-step approval process required before any newly constructed or renovated space within the {occupancy} facility in {county} County may be placed into service or occupied by patients. Pursuant to Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-07, the facility must obtain: (1) a Certificate of Occupancy (CO) issued by the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (the local building department) confirming that the construction meets the adopted local building code; and (2) a completed ODH on-site survey by an ODH Healthcare Surveyor confirming that the completed space meets all applicable ODH licensing regulations before the facility begins providing services from that space. Neither approval alone is sufficient — both must be obtained before patients may be seen in the new or renovated area. ODH will schedule the on-site survey only after the facility notifies ODH in writing that construction is complete and a local CO has been issued. Occupying or providing services in a space before both approvals are obtained is a licensing violation under Ohio Revised Code §3702.30.
fix_template:
1. Upon substantial completion of construction, schedule and pass all required inspections with the local building department; obtain the final Certificate of Occupancy (CO) or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) from the local AHJ and retain the original for the facility's permanent records.
2. Upon receipt of the local CO or TCO, notify the ODH Healthcare Regulatory Section in writing — including the ODH facility license number, name of the licensed administrator, a description of the completed space, and a copy of the local CO — to request an ODH on-site licensure survey; allow a minimum of 30 days for ODH to schedule the survey.
3. Ensure the facility is fully ready for the ODH survey before the survey date: all equipment is installed and operational, staff are trained and in place, required policies and procedures are in place, and the space is furnished and ready for patient use; a survey finding of substantial non-compliance will require a repeat survey and may delay licensure.
4. Do not allow patients to occupy the new or renovated space, or to receive services from it, until the ODH Surveyor has provided written notice of a satisfactory survey outcome and ODH has issued an amended or updated facility license covering the new space or service.
5. Retain copies of the local CO, ODH survey report, and the updated ODH license in the facility's permanent regulatory compliance files and make them available for inspection upon request by ODH or any accreditation body.

description: Sterile compounding pharmacy must comply with USP Chapter 797; negative pressure ISO 7 cleanroom required for hazardous drug compounding
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / STERILE COMPOUNDING (OH-PHARM-001): The construction documents submitted for the sterile compounding pharmacy within the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with USP General Chapter <797> (Pharmaceutical Compounding — Sterile Preparations) as required by the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy (OSBP) and referenced by Ohio Administrative Code 3715-27, or with applicable ODH facility design requirements. The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) the pharmacy cleanroom suite does not clearly demonstrate ISO 7 (Class 10,000) or better air cleanliness classification for the buffer room where sterile preparations are compounded, with continuous positive pressure maintained with respect to the ante-room and adjacent non-classified areas for non-hazardous compounds; (2) for any space designated for Category 1 or Category 2 sterile hazardous drug (HD) compounding, the construction documents do not specify a negative-pressure ISO 7 buffer room with a positive-pressure ISO 7 ante-room, with all HD room exhaust discharged directly to the building exterior through HEPA filtration; and/or (3) the air-balance schedule and room pressure diagrams required to verify cleanroom pressure cascades are not included in the mechanical submission. Failure to design the compounding pharmacy to USP <797> standards may result in denial of the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy operating license and ODH facility approval.
fix_template:
1. Classify each cleanroom space in the pharmacy suite by ISO cleanroom classification (ISO 5, ISO 7, or ISO 8) on the architectural floor plan; confirm the buffer room(s) achieve ISO 7 at a minimum and that a primary engineering control (PEC) with ISO 5 conditions (laminar airflow hood or biological safety cabinet) is located within the buffer room.
2. For non-hazardous sterile compounding: specify the buffer room at a continuous positive pressure differential of at least +0.02 to +0.05 inches water gauge (5–12.5 Pa) relative to the ante-room, and the ante-room at positive pressure relative to the adjacent general pharmacy or corridor; provide a pressure-cascade diagram on the mechanical drawings.
3. For hazardous drug (HD) sterile compounding: specify the HD buffer room at a continuous negative pressure of at least -0.01 to -0.03 inches water gauge (-2.5 to -7.5 Pa) relative to the ante-room, and the ante-room at positive pressure relative to the adjacent corridor; provide dedicated HEPA-filtered exhaust for the HD buffer room discharging directly to the building exterior; confirm no recirculation of HD room exhaust air to any other space.
4. Update the air-balance schedule to list supply CFM, exhaust CFM, net pressure, total ACH, and ISO classification for each cleanroom space; confirm a minimum of 30 ACPH (air changes per hour) in each ISO 7 buffer room per USP <797> Table 5 and FGI Guidelines recommendations; include a room-by-room pressure-cascade diagram as a dedicated mechanical drawing sheet.
5. Coordinate the pharmacy construction documents with the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy (OSBP) registration requirements under OAC 4729-17 and provide ODH with a copy of the OSBP facility registration or pre-application correspondence; resubmit revised mechanical drawings and pharmacy floor plan to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for review and approval.
